author: deseltrus
body:
## Problem

When the planner writes roadmap slices using heading-bullet-checkbox hybrid format (e.g., `### - [ ] S01 — Feature Title`), the roadmap parser returns 0 slices. This causes `deriveState()` to return `phase: pre-planning` even though a complete roadmap exists, triggering an infinite plan-milestone dispatch loop.

The format is a realistic LLM output — the planner combines H3 heading markers with markdown bullet-checkbox syntax. Neither the checkbox parser nor the prose header fallback can handle it.

## Root Cause

**File:** `roadmap-slices.ts`, function `parseProseSliceHeaders()`

The prose header regex expects the slice ID (`S01`) to appear immediately after heading markers and optional bold/checkmark tokens. It has no allowance for a `- ` bullet prefix or `[ ]/[x]` checkbox between the heading and the slice ID.

Lines like `### - [ ] S01 — Title` fail both parsers:
1. **Checkbox parser** — requires `- [ ]` at line start, blocked by `### ` prefix
2. **Prose parser** — doesn't allow `- [ ] ` between heading and slice ID

## Fix

Two surgical changes in `parseProseSliceHeaders()`:

1. **Regex**: Added optional non-capturing groups for the bullet-checkbox prefix, plus bare-checkbox-without-bullet (covers the pattern from #2053/#2263 as well)

2. **Done detection**: Added `checkboxDonePattern` so `### - [x] S01` correctly sets `done: true`

No capture group indices changed — all new groups are non-capturing.

**Patterns now handled:**

| Format | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `### - [ ] S01 — Title` | miss | done=false |
| `### - [x] S01 — Title` | miss | done=true |
| `### - S01 — Title` | miss | done=false |
| `### [x] S01 — Title` | miss | done=true |
| `## - [ ] S01 — Title` | miss | done=false |
| `### S01 — Title` | unchanged | unchanged |
| `- [ ] **S01: Title**` | unchanged | unchanged (checkbox parser) |

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/resources/extensions/gsd/roadmap-slices.ts` | Extended `headerPattern` regex and added `checkboxDonePattern` for done detection |
| `src/resources/extensions/gsd/tests/roadmap-parse-regression.test.ts` | Added section U with 4 test blocks (13 new assertions) covering bullet-checkbox, bullet-only, bare-checkbox, and H2 variants |

## Test Evidence

- All 20 `roadmap-slices.test.ts` tests pass
- All 87 `roadmap-parse-regression.test.ts` tests pass (74 existing + 13 new)
- `npm run build` succeeds

**Reproduction:** Create a roadmap with slices formatted as `### - [ ] S01 — Title` under a `## Slices` section. `parseRoadmapSlices()` returns 0 slices, `deriveState()` returns `phase: pre-planning`, auto-mode loops on plan-milestone indefinitely.

## Related

- Related to #2053 — prose header checkbox parsing (this PR also handles that pattern)
- Related to #2206 — `[x]` checkbox in H3/H4 prose headers
- Overlaps with PR #2265 — that PR handles `### [x] S01` but not `### - [ ] S01` (bullet prefix). This PR covers both patterns.

author: dhruvhaldar
body:
💡 What: Wrapped the GLTF node extraction (`Object.values(nodes).find(...)`) in `useMemo` hooks inside the `CFDModel` component.

🎯 Why: In React Three Fiber, component functions can run frequently (especially if a parent renders). `Object.values()` creates a new array on every call, and `.find()` iterates through it. Running this O(n) operation continuously on static GLTF nodes causes unnecessary memory allocations and CPU overhead, leading to Garbage Collection pauses.

📊 Impact: Prevents O(n) array allocations and lookups per render of the CFDModel. Reduces memory pressure and prevents potential micro-stutters during 3D scene interactions.

🔬 Measurement: Verified using a Playwright test scrolling through the page. The app loads cleanly without the HMR "too many hooks" error that triggered on the initial dev server test, and lint/tests pass seamlessly.

author: bestekarx
body:
## Summary

The existing `slim`, `normal`, and `json` formats for `adt git-diff` output file statistics and hunk headers but **omit the actual changed lines** (the `+`/`-` patch content). This makes it impossible for AI agents to understand *what* changed in the code — only *which files* changed.

This PR adds a new `--fmt full` format that includes:
- A compact summary header (`files: N  +X -Y`)
- The complete unified diff content (same as `git diff` output)

### Use case

AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.) need to read actual code diffs for tasks like:
- **Commit message generation** — understanding what changed, not just which files
- **Code review** — analyzing the actual modifications
- **Pre-commit checks** — verifying coding standards in changed lines

Without `--fmt full`, agents must fall back to raw `git diff`, losing the structured header and token estimation that `adt` provides.

### Usage

```bash
adt git-diff --fmt full          # unstaged changes with full patch
adt git-diff --staged --fmt full # staged changes with full patch
```

### Changes

- `src/types/index.ts` — Added `'full'` to `OutputFormat` type
- `src/core/format.ts` — Added `toFull()` method and `'full'` case to output/error switches
- `src/commands/git/diff.ts` — Added `'full'` format branch in `formatDiff()` that outputs the raw diff content

### Token comparison

| Format | Output size | Content |
|--------|------------|---------|
| `slim` | ~155 tokens | File list + stats only |
| `normal` | ~156 tokens | File list + line counts |
| **`full`** | **~4,173 tokens** | Header + complete diff |
| `git diff` | ~4,180 tokens | Raw diff (no header) |

`full` ≈ raw `git diff` + structured header. The token cost is the same as running `git diff` directly, but with the benefit of adt's consistent output format and token estimation.

## Test plan

- [x] `adt git-diff --fmt full` shows complete diff with header
- [x] `adt git-diff --staged --fmt full` works for staged changes
- [x] `adt git-diff --fmt slim` still works (no regression)
- [x] `adt git-diff --fmt normal` still works (no regression)
- [x] Build succeeds with `npm run build`

author: milanrada
body:
## Summary

- **Fix doubled navigation bar**: `dismissCoordinator()` now cleans up own pushed destinations when the parent chain cannot be fully dismissed (e.g. parent is a tab child or RootCoordinatable with no grandparent). Previously, stale destinations remained in the flattened `NavigationStack` path, causing a doubled navigation bar.
- **Break retain cycles**: Make `parent` references `weak` in `FlowStack`, `TabItems`, and `Root`. Add `AnyObject` constraint to `Coordinatable` protocol (all coordinators are already classes via `@Observable`). Previously, the strong `parent` references created cycles: `Parent → Stack → Destination → Cache → Child → Stack.parent → Parent`.
- **Fix orphaned destinations**: `dismissCoordinator()` now uses `removeSubrange(selfIndex...)` instead of `removeAll(where:)` to also remove plain-view destinations that were pushed on top of the dismissed coordinator.
- **Remove dead code**: The `else if originalDestination.pushType == .push` branch in `reconstructDestinations` was unreachable when `presentationType == .push` (the only call site from `bindingStack`).

## Reproduction scenario (doubled navigation bar)

1. `FlowCoordinatorA` is the **root** of `FlowCoordinatorB` (its parent)
2. `FlowCoordinatorB` is a tab child (parent is a `TabCoordinatable`)
3. Screens are pushed onto `FlowCoordinatorA`'s stack
4. `dismissCoordinator()` is called on `FlowCoordinatorA`
5. `dismissCoordinator()` detects it is the root → calls `parent.dismissCoordinator()` on `FlowCoordinatorB`
6. `FlowCoordinatorB.dismissCoordinator()` detects parent is `TabCoordinatable` → silently fails
7. **Before fix**: `FlowCoordinatorA`'s pushed destinations remain in the flattened `NavigationStack` path → doubled navigation bar
8. **After fix**: `FlowCoordinatorA`'s destinations are cleared as fallback cleanup

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Coordinatable.swift` | Add `AnyObject` to protocol, add fallback cleanup in `dismissCoordinator()`, use `removeSubrange` |
| `FlowStack.swift` | `weak var parent` |
| `TabItems.swift` | `weak var parent` |
| `Root.swift` | `weak var parent` |
| `FlowCoordinatable.swift` | Remove ~70 lines of unreachable dead code in `reconstructDestinations` |

author: ddklo
body:
Previously, safeRoute for non-backtrack levels stored only one waypoint
per row: {row: R, col: safePath[R]}. The path highlight drew arrows
directly from (R, A) to (R+1, B) when A≠B, which looks like an illegal
diagonal jump. In reality, a forward jump always lands at the player's
current column in the next row (nearest platform), then hops bring the
player to the destination column.

Expand safeRoute to include every individual move:
- Forward jump step: {row: r, col: prevCol} (where player actually lands)
- Hop steps: {row: r, col: prevCol+1}, ..., {row: r, col: destCol}

The bridge already guarantees all intermediate columns in the destination
row are real, so these steps are always safe platforms.

This means drawPathReveal now shows only vertical arrows (forward jumps,
same column) and horizontal arrows (hops, same row ±1), eliminating all
illegal-looking diagonal arrows and correctly representing the optimal path.

Update tests: safeRoute.length is now ≥ gridRows (not == gridRows), add
validation that every consecutive step pair is a legal move, verify
intermediate hop platforms are real.

author: bogenbai
body:
Entitas-Flux v0.0.5

Added

- HasEntityIndex / RemoveEntityIndex on Context  
  New API methods on IContext and Context to check whether an entity index exists and to remove (with deactivation) an entity index by name. Includes full test coverage.

- Watched component introspection API  
  New WatchedEntityHasChangedGenerator that generates per-entity helper methods for watched components:
    - HasChanged(int componentId) — whether a watched component has changed
    - ComponentIsChangedFlag(int componentId) — whether a component ID is a "Changed" flag
    - GetOriginalComponentIdFromChangeFlag(int flagId) — resolves a flag back to its source component
    - IsWatchedComponent(int componentId) — whether a component is watched
    - GetChangedFlagIdOf(int componentId) — gets the flag ID for a watched component
    - GetChangeFlagTypeOf(int componentId) — gets the flag Type for a watched component

- Unity inspector triggers [Watched] change markers  
  Adding, removing, or editing a watched component through the Unity inspector now correctly adds the corresponding {Component}Changed marker component.


Fixed

- [DontGenerate] components still generated code  
  Components marked with [DontGenerate] were still producing generated output. Both reflection and Roslyn data providers now fully skip these components.

- EntityIndexGenerator generated for [DontGenerate] components  
  Entity index data providers (both reflection and Roslyn) now filter out [DontGenerate] components. Includes test fixture and tests.

- Primary index components with the same name but different contexts caused generation errors  
  EntityIndexGenerator now deduplicates index constant names via .Distinct().

- Watched component generated in one context only  
  When a [Watched] component belonged to multiple contexts, the generated {Component}Changed marker was only assigned to the first context. Both ComponentDataProvider implementations now merge context names across duplicates.

- Generated [Watched] component context order was non-deterministic  
  Context names on watched marker components are now sorted alphabetically for stable output.

- Generated cleanup systems order was non-deterministic  
  Both CleanupSystemsGenerator and WatchedCleanupSystemsGenerator now sort by context name and component name, producing deterministic output across builds.

author: zszabo-rh
body:
[MGMT-23330](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MGMT-23330)

## Summary
Replace ad-hoc goroutine management with errgroup, following the multicluster-runtime official example pattern.

## Problem

The operator starts three blocking components concurrently (remote cluster, remote provider, manager) with inconsistent error handling:
- remoteCluster.Start() called os.Exit(1) on failure — abrupt termination, defers skipped, no cleanup
- remoteProvider.Start() silently swallowed errors — operator continued running with a broken provider
- No coordinated shutdown between components

## Solution
All three components now run as errgroup goroutines with a shared cancellable context:
- If any component returns an error, errgroup cancels the context, triggering graceful shutdown of the others
- context.Canceled errors are filtered via ignoreCanceled() since they represent normal shutdown, not failures
- Provider errors now surface through errgroup instead of being silently logged

Startup ordering (cache sync before controller workers) is handled internally by multicluster-runtime's WaitForSync on registered syncing sources — no explicit barrier needed in main().

## Changes
Commit 1 — Implementation:
- Replace raw goroutines + os.Exit(1) with errgroup.WithContext
- Add ignoreCanceled() helper (same as multicluster-runtime example)

Commit 2 — Tests:
- Extract startup orchestration into testable startComponents() function
- Add 10 tests covering error propagation, graceful shutdown, and component failure cascading
- cmd package coverage: 0.0% → 4.5%

## Test plan
- Unit tests pass (make build — all suites green)
- New tests: go test ./cmd/ -v — 10/10 pass
- E2E: deployed on hypershift1, operator starts cleanly, all controllers running, tenant reconciled successfully
- Remote-cluster mode not E2E tested (requires dual-cluster setup)

author: salhik
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: rayrayraykk
body:
Refactors Feishu channel implementation to use native async methods instead of synchronous calls wrapped in thread pool executors, resulting in better performance, reduced resource usage, and cleaner code.
**Key Changes**:
- 🚀 Replace all `run_in_executor` calls with native async SDK methods
- ⚡ Migrate from `urllib.request` to `httpx.AsyncClient` for HTTP requests
- 🧹 Remove 3 synchronous wrapper methods (`_add_reaction_sync`, `_upload_image_sync`, `_send_message_sync`)
- 🎯 Use Lark SDK's async methods (`acreate`, `aget`) throughout
**Net Effect**: Eliminated 6 thread pool calls, removed 3 wrapper methods, improved async performance
---
## Changes
### 1. HTTP Request Optimization
#### Migrate to httpx.AsyncClient
- ✅ **`_fetch_bot_open_id()`**: Replace `urllib.request.urlopen()` with `httpx.AsyncClient.get()`
  - Cleaner async/await syntax
  - Better timeout and error handling
  
- ✅ **`_fetch_bytes_from_url()`**: Replace `urllib.request.urlopen()` with `httpx.AsyncClient.get()`
  - Consistent HTTP client usage across the codebase
  - Native async I/O without blocking
### 2. Lark SDK Async Integration
#### Message Operations
- ✅ **`_send_message_sync()` → `_send_message()`**
  - Changed from `im.v1.message.create()` to `im.v1.message.acreate()`
  - Removed `_sync` suffix as it's now truly async
  - Eliminated `run_in_executor` wrapper in `_send_text()`
#### Reaction Operations
- ✅ **Merged `_add_reaction()` and `_add_reaction_sync()`**
  - Single async method using `im.v1.message_reaction.acreate()`
  - Direct async call, no thread pool overhead
  - Simplified from 2 methods to 1
#### Image Operations
- ✅ **`_upload_image_sync()` → `_upload_image()`**
  - Changed from `im.v1.image.create()` to `im.v1.image.acreate()`
  - Removed `_sync` suffix
  - Updated caller in `_send_image()` to remove executor wrapper
- ✅ **`_download_image_resource()`**
  - Changed from `im.v1.message_resource.get()` to `im.v1.message_resource.aget()`
  - Added `asyncio.to_thread()` for file I/O operations
#### File Operations
- ✅ **`_upload_file()`**
  - Changed from `im.v1.file.create()` to `im.v1.file.acreate()`
  - Added `asyncio.to_thread()` for file I/O operations (`write_bytes`, `stat`, `open`)
  - Updated caller in `_send_file()` to remove executor wrapper
- ✅ **`_download_file_resource()`**
  - Changed from `im.v1.message_resource.get()` to `im.v1.message_resource.aget()`
  - Added `asyncio.to_thread()` for file I/O operations
### 3. Code Cleanup
#### Removed Methods
- ❌ `_add_reaction_sync()` - merged into `_add_reaction()`
- ❌ `_upload_image_sync()` - renamed to `_upload_image()` with async implementation
- ❌ `_send_message_sync()` - renamed to `_send_message()` with async implementation
#### Simplified Call Sites
- ✅ `_send_text()`: Removed lambda wrapping and executor calls
- ✅ `_send_image()`: Direct async method calls
- ✅ `_send_file()`: Direct async method calls
---
## Technical Details
### Before: Thread Pool Executor Pattern
```python
# Old pattern - unnecessary thread pool overhead
loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
result = await loop.run_in_executor(
    None,
    lambda: self._client.im.v1.message.create(req),
)
```
### After: Native Async Pattern
```python
# New pattern - native async SDK call
result = await self._client.im.v1.message.acreate(req)
```
### HTTP Request Evolution
**Before:**
```python
req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={...})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
    data = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
```
**After:**
```python
async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
    response = await client.get(url, headers={...})
    data = response.json()
```
### File I/O Considerations
For blocking file operations that cannot be made async at SDK level:
```python
# Use asyncio.to_thread for blocking I/O
await asyncio.to_thread(path.write_bytes, data)
await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: path.stat().st_size)
file_obj = await asyncio.to_thread(path.open, "rb")
```
---
## Performance Impact
### Before Optimization
Each Feishu API call required:
1. Get event loop reference
2. Submit to thread pool executor
3. Thread scheduling and context switch
4. Synchronous blocking wait
5. Result return to main event loop
**Overhead per call**: ~1-5ms (thread pool overhead) + thread memory (stack allocation)
### After Optimization
Each Feishu API call:
1. Direct async method invocation
2. Coroutine scheduling (no thread switch)
3. Non-blocking await
4. Immediate result return
**Benefits**:
- ⚡ **Latency**: Reduced 1-5ms per API call
- 🚀 **Concurrency**: No thread pool limits, unlimited concurrent requests
- 💾 **Memory**: Reduced memory footprint (no extra thread stacks)
- 🎯 **Scalability**: Better performance under high message throughput
---
## Benefits
1. **Performance**: Native async I/O eliminates thread pool overhead
2. **Code Quality**: Cleaner, more idiomatic async/await code
3. **Maintainability**: Fewer wrapper methods and less indirection
4. **Resource Efficiency**: Reduced thread usage and memory consumption
5. **Error Handling**: Better exception propagation in async context
6. **Consistency**: Uses httpx consistently with rest of the codebase

### Motivation
- Add milestone-1 Payment + Checkout capabilities so users can view a checkout summary and process payments for orders. 
- Provide server-side validation and safety checks around payment state transitions to avoid invalid or destructive updates. 
- Expose endpoints and tests to drive integration coverage for the checkout → order → payment flow.

## Summary

The goal for this PR is to display a native browser tooltip on Table cells whose content is truncated (short-text, url, long-text).

(Internal for Opendatasoft only) Associated Shortcut ticket: [sc-56458](https://app.shortcut.com/huwise/story/56458/table-better-display-and-readability-of-text-fields-with-many-characters).

### Changes

Introduces a `titleOnOverflow` Svelte action in a new `actions.ts` file.
The action listens to `mouseenter` and sets the `title` attribute only when the cell content is actually clipped (detected by comparing `scrollWidth`/ `scrollHeight` against `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight` on the cell's first child element or the cell div itself. The action is applied to the `cell-content` wrapper div in `CellContent.svelte`.

#### Breaking Changes

None.

### Changelog

In the Table component: cells with truncated content now display a native tooltip on hover, showing the full text.

## Open discussion

The overflow detection relies on `firstElementChild` to handle the `long-text` case rather than on the cell div directly. If the DOM structure of a cell type changes, the detection logic may need to be updated.

## To be tested

- **short-text**: hover a cell whose text is cut off with an ellipsis → tooltip appears
- **url**: same as short-text
- **long-text**: hover a cell whose text is clamped to 3 lines → tooltip appears
- No tooltip should appear when the content is **not** truncated (cell wide enough)

## Summary

Changes the reroll-stop condition in `RerollStart` so that when both investment environment and investment strategy are configured, satisfying **either** condition (OR) stops the reroll loop — previously **both** had to be satisfied (AND). Boss name/affix checks remain AND as before.

Key changes in `tasks/currency_wars/RerollStart.py`:
- Added `self.invest_env_satisfied` flag to track whether the investment environment matched
- `handle_invest_environment`: sets the flag on match; removed `self.reroll = True` when env doesn't match (env mismatch alone no longer triggers immediate reroll)
- `handle_game_entered`: restructured decision tree — if env satisfied, stop immediately (OR short-circuit); if env not satisfied and no strategy config, abort; if env not satisfied but strategy config exists, continue to let strategy check run

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Stale `invest_env_satisfied` across reroll cycles**: The flag is set to `True` when env matches but is **never reset to `False`** after an abort. If cycle N matches env but fails boss check → abort → cycle N+1 has a different env that doesn't match, the stale `True` flag would incorrectly stop the reroll. Compare with `self.reroll` which IS reset after abort. Consider whether `invest_env_satisfied` (and possibly `invest_strategy_satisfied`, `invest_strategy_stage`) need to be reset in the abort path.
- [ ] **Verify call order in parent class `CurrencyWars`**: Confirm that `handle_boss_info` → `handle_invest_environment` → `handle_game_entered` is the actual execution order, since the correctness of the new branching logic depends on this sequence.
- [ ] **Test scenario: only env configured (no strategy)** — env doesn't match → should abort and retry. Env matches → should stop.
- [ ] **Test scenario: both env and strategy configured** — env matches → should stop immediately without checking strategy. Env doesn't match, strategy matches later → should stop at `handle_stage_transitioned`.
- [ ] **Test scenario: only strategy configured (no env)** — behavior should be unchanged from before this PR.

Recommend running the Currency Wars reroll automation with various combinations of `invest_env` / `invest_strategy` settings against the live game to verify all paths.

### Notes
- No automated tests exist for this module; changes can only be verified via manual testing with the game client.
- `handle_invest_strategy` and `handle_stage_transitioned` are intentionally unchanged per requirements.

Test 7 was manually constructing `MarketTradeUpdate` with a hardcoded `Venue: "NYSE"` for both AAPL records, bypassing the actual `NyseNationalTradesCsvParser` → `NyseMarketDataClient.OnTrade` mapping. The two golden-sample lines carry different exchange codes (5 = NYSE, 6 = EDGX) and therefore land on independent `(symbol, streamId, venue)` collector tracks — not a shared one.

- **Test 7 rewritten** — now calls `ToUpdate(record)` for both records, routing them through the real exchange-code mapping. Assertions updated to reflect per-venue state isolation:
  - NYSE track (code 5, 3 shares @ 171.08): VWAP = 171.08

author: jscheid
body:
Strategy error handlers were stringifying errors via `inspect()` before storing them in the result field. This destroyed the structured error information, making it impossible for consumers to pattern-match on specific error types (e.g. HTTP 503 with a provider message).

Store the original error term directly. The `Snapshot.result` field is typed as `any()` so this is compatible with the existing contract.

Applies to `ReAct`, `ChainOfThought`, and `ChainOfDraft` strategies.

This is a breaking change affecting any code that reads `snapshot.result` after a failure and assumes it is a binary. The most common patterns:
1. String matching (`result =~ "..."`, `String.contains?/2`): Replace with pattern matching on the term. E.g. `result =~ "rate_limited"` becomes `result == :rate_limited`.
2. Display / logging (`Logger.error("Failed: #{result}")`): Wrap with `inspect/1` at the display boundary. E.g. `"Failed: #{inspect(result)}"`.
3. Guard clauses (`when is_binary(result)`): Update to handle the actual term type, or remove the guard and match structurally.
4. Downstream of `Request.await/2`: The third element of `{:failed, reason, result}` tuples returned via `failure_reason/1` carries the same change. Consumers that destructure this tuple and assume a string need updating.

author: uatec
body:
## Root Cause

The `TvPowerOn` event handler called `ChangeInputToThisDeviceAsync()` (cec-client `as` command) whenever an "Image View On" or "Text View On" message appeared on the CEC bus. The `as` command sends both **Active Source** and **Image View On** — and Image View On is a power-on command. So a stray CEC bus event after standby would trigger Baird to tell the TV to turn on, creating a feedback loop.

The ~10-minute delay matches the time for a stray CEC bus event (TV standby housekeeping, another device polling) to appear after the TV powers off. Once the TV turned on, `InputRegained` fired → `UnblockInputs()` resumed the paused video → noise on the right input.

There was also a secondary bug: `commandType.Contains("Active Source")` matched both "Active Source" (0x82) and "Request Active Source" (0x85), causing `InputLost` and `InputRegained` to fire on the same event.

## Changes

- **TvPowerOn handler**: no longer sends any CEC commands (was the feedback loop)
- **CEC startup**: no longer sends `as` (was powering TV on after app restart)
- **AssertCecPresence**: removed `PowerOnAsync`, keeps `ChangeInputToThisDeviceAsync` (only fires on actual human input with 30s cooldown)
- **InputRegained**: no longer auto-resumes video (was triggered by stray bus events)
- **Video resume**: moved to `ResumeAfterStandby()`, called only from key/pointer input handlers
- **Idle timer**: skips screensaver when TV is in standby
- **CecService**: fixed `Contains("Active Source")` incorrectly matching "Request Active Source"
- **Removed all dead input blocking code** (`_inputsBlocked`, `_inputLockDisabled`, `_inputUnblockFallbackTimer`, `RequestInputRegain()`, `UnblockInputs()`) — `_inputLockDisabled` was hardcoded to `true` so none of this code ever ran

## Test plan

- [ ] Turn off TV with TV remote — verify it stays off indefinitely
- [ ] Turn TV back on manually, press a button — verify Baird claims active source and resumes video
- [ ] Let app sit idle with TV off — verify screensaver does not activate
- [ ] Restart app while TV is off — verify TV is not powered on

author: deepjoy
body:
## Summary

- **Priority aging (phase 1):** Tasks waiting longer than a configurable grace period are gradually promoted in effective priority at dispatch time, preventing starvation of low-priority work under sustained high-priority load. The stored priority is never mutated — effective priority is computed in SQL via the aging formula. Pause duration is excluded from the aging clock so paused tasks don't get unfair promotion.
- **Weighted fair scheduling (phase 2):** Three-pass dispatch loop allocates slots proportional to per-group weights, fills remaining capacity greedily, and dispatches urgently-aged tasks as a safety valve. Ungrouped tasks compete as a virtual group with the default weight. Min-slots guarantees and concurrency caps are respected. Work-conserving by construction.
- **Composes with existing features:** Rate limits, group pause, concurrency caps, preemption, and backpressure all interact correctly. Fast dispatch is disabled when aging or weights are configured.

Closes #37 
### New public API

| Builder | Runtime | Event |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `priority_aging(AgingConfig)` | — | `base_priority` / `effective_priority` on `TaskEventHeader` |
| `group_weight(group, weight)` | `set_group_weight(group, weight)` | `GroupWeightChanged` |
| `default_group_weight(weight)` | `remove_group_weight(group)` | — |
| `group_minimum_slots(group, slots)` | `reset_group_weights()` | — |
| — | `set_group_minimum_slots(group, slots)` | — |

### New store queries

`peek_next_in_group()`, `peek_next_ungrouped()`, `running_counts_per_group()`, `pending_counts_per_group()`, `peek_next_urgent()`

### Schema changes (pre-1.0, inline)

`pause_duration_ms INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and `paused_at_ms INTEGER DEFAULT NULL` added to `tasks` table for aging clock management.

author: weareu
body:
## Problem

Using DroidClaw with OpenRouter (or any Azure-backed provider) fails with:

```
AI_APICallError: [Azure] Invalid schema for response_format 'response':
[{'type': 'number'}, {'type': 'number'}] is not of type 'object', 'boolean'
```

This happens because `z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])` serializes to JSON Schema tuple validation:
```json
{"type": "array", "items": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "number"}]}
```

Azure's structured output rejects tuple schemas — it only supports single-schema `items`.

## Fix

Replace `z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])` with `z.array(z.number()).min(2).max(2)`.

This produces universally compatible JSON Schema:
```json
{"type": "array", "items": {"type": "number"}, "minItems": 2, "maxItems": 2}
```

Same runtime constraint (exactly 2 numbers), works with all providers.

## Tested with

- OpenRouter → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (was failing, now works)
- OpenRouter → `openai/gpt-4o` (was failing, now works)

Fixes #26690

## Summary

- When an entity is created and immediately hard-deleted, async event consumers (`WorkflowEventConsumer`, `ActivityFeedPublisher`) throw `EntityNotFoundException` because the entity is gone by the time they process the create event

author: naveensandaruwan
body:
## Purpose
> This PR introduces a Semantic Tool Filtering Policy for the WSO2 AI Gateway to solve the problem of "tool over-exposure" in Agentic applications. Currently, exposing all available tools (50-100+) to an LLM leads to degraded performance, increased risk of hallucinations, and high token costs.

## Goals
>  - Reduce LLM Hallucinations: Minimize the "search space" to improve the mathematical probability of correct tool selection.
> - Optimize Performance: Prevent context window overflow and reduce system latency by sending only relevant content to the LLM.
> - Cost Efficiency: Lower token usage by filtering out irrelevant tool descriptions before request reach to LLM .

## Approach
> The policy implements a semantic retrieval and caching process:

> 1. Semantic Ranking: Converts the user query and tool metadata into high-dimensional vectors to calculate Cosine Similarity.
> 2. Dynamic Filtering: Injects only the top-ranked tools (e.g., top 5) into the LLM prompt.
> 3. Caching Mechanism: Uses a hashing strategy to store tool embeddings in a vector database. This avoids redundant embedding generation for recurring tool descriptions at runtime.

## User stories
> As a developer building sophisticated Agentic applications, I want the AI Gateway to automatically select the most relevant tools for a user's request so that the application remains fast, accurate, and cost-effective even as my toolset grows.

## Samples

![Semantic tool filtering process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad859e1b-9644-4641-8c43-ef9b45be4671)

author: iwhite67
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/French-CSGO/G5API/security/code-scanning/128](https://github.com/French-CSGO/G5API/security/code-scanning/128)

In general, to fix uncontrolled path usage, normalize the path relative to a trusted root directory and then verify that the normalized path is still within that root. Alternatively, restrict user-controlled values to *identifiers* (not paths) and use them only in safe positions like directory names or filenames, while keeping the path structure itself hard-coded.

For this specific code, the safest and simplest approach without changing functionality is:

1. Treat `backupRoot` (`public/backups`) as the only root.
2. Keep `matchId`, `mapNumber`, and `roundNumber` as identifiers (we already validate them with strict regexes).
3. Construct a filename string that is entirely under our control except for these validated identifiers.
4. Combine everything with `path.join(backupRoot, matchId, filename)` and then:
   - Use `path.resolve` to normalize the final path.
   - Verify that this final path starts with the canonical `backupRoot` path (plus separator).
5. Remove the incorrect check comparing a file path to `matchDir`.

This preserves behavior (still writes backups under `public/backups/<matchId>/...`) but uses one clear, canonical containment check at the root level. It also keeps the data flow pattern simple enough that CodeQL can see the validation and containment.

Concretely in `src/routes/v2/backupapi.ts`:

- Keep the existing regex validation for `matchId`, `mapNumber`, and `roundNumber`.
- Define `backupRoot` with `path.resolve("public", "backups")` as already done.
- Remove `resolvedBackupFilePath` and the associated check.
- Instead, after constructing `backupFilePath` with `path.join`, call `path.resolve(backupFilePath)` to get `resolvedBackupFilePath`.
- Check that `resolvedBackupFilePath` starts with `backupRoot + path.sep` (or equals `backupRoot` if we ever allowed directories).
- Use `resolvedBackupFilePath` directly in `writeFile`.

No new imports are needed; we already import `path` and `fs` helpers.

body:
This PR removes the `materialized_view` materialization and improves the behavior when tables already exist.

- **`materialized_view` materialization**: Now raises a compilation error directing users to use `table` instead, since in Confluent Flink both are implemented as CTAS tables
- **Skip instead of error on existing relations**: When a table/streaming_table/streaming_source already exists, skip recreation with a log message instead of raising an error (unless `--full-refresh` is specified)
- **Unified helper macro**: Renamed `drop_if_full_refresh()` to `skip_or_drop_existing()` to better reflect the new behavior

The current skip-on-existing behavior is intentionally simple. A follow-up PR (already prepared) will add schema drift detection that compares the existing relation's schema against the expected definition and fails if they differ, preventing silent schema mismatches.

body:
## Summary
This PR implements the full NT-24 story for staff queue operations in Sprint 3.

Staff users can now:
- serve the current queue head
- skip the current queue head as no-show (with optional reason)
- automatically advance the queue after each action
- generate auditable records for each serve/skip action

The implementation follows the modular monolith + Clean Architecture conventions:
- business rules in Application/Domain
- thin controller endpoints
- tenant-aware authorization checks
- FluentValidation for command inputs
- audit persistence in Infrastructure
- unit + integration + frontend tests added/updated

---

## Story Coverage

### User Story
As a staff member (tenant-scoped user), I want to mark the next queue entry as served or skipped so the queue advances and actions are audited.

### Implemented Endpoints
- `POST /api/queues/{queueId}/serve-next`
- `POST /api/queues/{queueId}/skip`

### Authorization & Tenant Rules
- Endpoint access restricted to authenticated `Staff` role
- Queue assignment is enforced before action execution
- Tenant context and assignment checks are applied before command dispatch

---

## What Changed

### 1. Application Layer (CQRS + Validation)
Added new commands, handlers, and validators for:
- `ServeNext`
- `Skip` (with optional reason, max 200 chars)

Behavior:
- Queue head resolution:
  - use current `Serving` entry when present
  - otherwise use next `Waiting` entry
- `ServeNext` transitions target entry to `Served`
- `Skip` transitions target entry to `NoShow`
- Both commands write audit log entries in same request flow

### 2. API Layer
Added new controller actions:
- `serve-next`
- `skip`

Added request contract for skip:
- optional `reason` payload

Controller remains thin:
- claim extraction
- assignment check
- MediatR command dispatch
- response mapping

### 3. Domain + Infrastructure Audit Logging
Introduced queue action audit model and enum for action type:
- action type (`Serve` / `Skip`)
- performed by user id
- queue id
- queue entry id
- timestamp
- reason (skip only, optional)

Added EF Core mapping and tenant query filter support.
Added EF migration for the audit table and updated model snapshot.

### 4. Frontend (Staff Dashboard + API Client)
Updated staff dashboard flow to use:
- `serve-next`
- `skip`

Updated queue API client methods accordingly.
Updated UI test coverage for:
- serving queue head
- skipping queue head with reason
- disabled action state when no actionable entry

---

## Behavioral Notes
- Skip sets status to `NoShow` (as requested)
- Queue progression is immediate in persisted state; dashboard refresh/poll picks up updated waiting positions
- Audit records are written for both actions and include required fields

---

## Testing

### Unit Tests
Added focused tests for:
- `ServeNextCommandHandler`
- `SkipCommandHandler`

Coverage includes:
- happy paths
- queue not found
- no active entry
- audit log insertion assertions
- skip reason handling

### Integration Tests
Extended staff queue integration tests to verify:
- DB state transition for serve/skip
- queue advancement effect
- audit row creation and values

### Frontend Tests
Updated Staff dashboard test suite to verify:
- serve-next action path
- skip action path with reason
- refresh behavior and disabled states

### Build/Test Results
- Solution build: pass
- New unit tests: pass
- Updated frontend tests: pass
- Integration tests are implemented; execution depends on local Docker/Testcontainers availability

---

## Commit Breakdown (Granular)
1. `feat(queue): add staff serve-next/skip actions with audit logging`
2. `test(queue): cover serve-next and skip handlers plus integration audit checks`
3. `feat(web): switch staff dashboard to serve-next and skip actions`

---

## Demo Steps
1. Login as Staff user assigned to a queue in a tenant
2. Open staff dashboard for that tenant
3. Trigger `Serve Next`
4. Trigger `Skip Next` with a reason
5. Verify queue head advances and waiting line updates on refresh/poll
6. Verify audit entries exist with:
   - action type
   - performedBy user id
   - queue id
   - queue entry id
   - timestamp
   - reason (for skip)

---

## Acceptance Criteria Mapping
- Staff-only + tenant-correct access: implemented
- `serve-next` endpoint: implemented
- `skip` endpoint with optional reason max 200: implemented
- Queue advancement and updated positions: implemented
- Audit log fields: implemented
- Proper error responses for invalid/not found/no active entry/forbidden: implemented via existing middleware + endpoint guards
- Unit + integration coverage for new logic: added

author: konard
body:
## Summary

Fixes xlab2016/space_db_private#23

Two bugs prevented `client_claw.agi` from compiling with the error "Expected body block for procedure 'call'" and subsequent errors.

### Root Cause 1: Member access from procedure parameter not registering result variable

When a procedure receives a parameter (e.g., `procedure call(data)`), the parameter is registered as a "global" kind variable. When the procedure body does `var command := data.command;`, the assignment path in `StatementLoweringCompiler` checked for kinds `"memory"`, `"stream"`, `"def"` but NOT `"global"`. As a result, the member access was silently skipped without registering `command` in `vars`, causing any subsequent use of `command` (e.g., `switch command { ... }`) to fail with "Cannot compile switch expression: 'command'".

**Fix:** Added `"global"` to the accepted kinds list and use `CreatePushGlobalMemoryInstruction` for global-kind variables.

### Root Cause 2: Format string `#"..."` not handled as print() argument

In `TryCompileFunctionCall`, when parsing `print(#"Hello world from Claw {socket1.name}")`, the `#` character was tokenized as a bare identifier. The code tried to look it up in `vars` and threw "Variable '#' is not declared".

**Fix:** Added detection of the `#` + StringLiteral token pair as a format string argument and compile it using the existing `TryParseFormatStringLiteral` + `TryCompileExpressionToSlot` infrastructure.

### Tests Added (`ClawLanguageFeaturesTests`)

- `CompileAsync_ProcedureWithMemberAccessFromParam_ShouldRegisterLocalVar` — regression test for bug 1
- `CompileAsync_ProcedureWithSwitchOnMemberAccessVar_ShouldCompileSuccessfully` — regression test for bug 1 with switch
- `CompileAsync_PrintWithFormatStringArgument_ShouldCompileSuccessfully` — regression test for bug 2
- `CompileAsync_FullClientClawPattern_ShouldCompileSuccessfully` — end-to-end test for the full `client_claw.agi` pattern

## Test plan

- [x] All 244 existing + new tests pass (`dotnet test Libs/Magic.Kernel.Tests/Magic.Kernel.Tests.csproj`)
- [x] `client_claw.agi` compiles successfully via `Magic.Compiler`

### What does this PR do?
Breaks the Go module dependency cycle between `pkg/config/create` and `pkg/config/structure` by removing test-only cross-imports. The cycle existed because tests in each module happened to use a convenience function from the other for test setup. No production code is changed.

### Motivation
The `datadog-agent` repository has ~190 internal Go modules. Bazel is using a Direct Acyclic Graph (**DAG**) — it cannot build modules with cyclic dependencies. A module dependency graph analysis identified 4 cycles blocking 73 modules from Bazel migration. This cycle blocks 57 downstream modules.

### Describe how you validated your changes
```shell
cd pkg/config/structure && go test ./...
cd pkg/config/create && go test ./...
cd pkg/config/create && go test -fuzz=FuzzReadConfig -fuzztime=5s ./...
go mod tidy # on both modules confirms config/create is no longer in structure/go.mod requires and vice versa
dda inv modules.add-all-replace
```

### Additional Notes
This is one of the 3 cycles to break for the Bazel migration.

author: zoechi
body:
## Summary

- Replace external `jj rebase -r '<name>@'` with internal `cd <path> && jj rebase -r @` for each workspace
- Add Step 3 to derive workspace root paths (`$WS_DIR`, `$MAIN_REPO`) before rebasing
- Add Notes bullet explaining the race condition: external rebase skips working-copy update, causing a reconcile op that can race with concurrent snapshots from an active session and drop uncommitted changes
- Bump plugin version 1.0.9 → 1.0.10

## Root cause

External rebase (`jj rebase -r 'ws@'`) rewrites the commit in the object store but does **not** update the working copy on disk. The workspace later detects staleness and runs a reconcile op. If another active session is concurrently snapshotting, this creates a divergent op chain — reconcile picks the rebase branch as winner, dropping the live snapshot and orphaning uncommitted changes.

Internal rebase (`cd <path> && jj rebase -r @`) is one atomic op: commit rewrite + working copy update together — no reconcile, no race window.

### Added
- JsonConfigurator for configuring logging from JSON files (`log4qt.json`).
  The JSON structure maps directly to flat property keys via dot-separated
  nesting. Automatic initialization searches for `log4qt.json` alongside
  `log4qt.properties` (`.properties` takes priority).
- XmlConfigurator for configuring logging from XML files (`log4qt.xml`).
  Nested elements produce dot-separated keys; XML attributes are flattened
  as child properties. Automatic initialization searches for `log4qt.xml`
  after `log4qt.json` (`.properties` > `.json` > `.xml` priority).
- Short factory aliases for all built-in components (e.g. `Console`,
  `File`, `RollingFile`, `PatternLayout`, `LevelMatch`) alongside the
  existing `org.apache.log4j.*` and `Log4Qt::*` names.
- Dedicated PropertyConfigurator unit test suite (`tests/propertytest`).

### Changed
- **Breaking:** Minimum required Qt version raised to Qt 6.4. Qt 5 is no longer
  supported. Use branch 1.6 / release 1.6.x for Qt 5.7+ support.
- **Breaking:** PropertyConfigurator now uses a Log4j2-style configuration
  format. The `log4j.` prefix is removed, appenders use explicit `type` keys,
  and loggers use appender references instead of inline declarations:
  - `log4j.rootLogger=ALL, console` → `rootLogger.level=ALL` +
    `rootLogger.appenderRef.0.ref=console`
  - `log4j.appender.X=org.apache.log4j.ConsoleAppender` →

  - `log4j.appender.X.layout=org.apache.log4j.TTCCLayout` →

  - `log4j.logger.MyApp=ERROR, console` → `logger.MyApp.name=MyApp` +

  - `log4j.additivity.MyApp=false` → `logger.MyApp.additivity=false`
  - Global settings: `log4j.reset` → `reset`, `log4j.Debug` →
    `status`, `log4j.threshold` → `threshold`, etc.
- Appender filters now configured via `appender.X.filter.F.type=LevelMatch`

author: nquarex
body:
### Motivation
- Telemetry was generating high-frequency network requests (heartbeat, pause/resume, periodic sends) that can slow or block the app, especially when Telegram is unavailable in some regions. 
- The intent is to preserve telemetry data but send it only at meaningful points so gameplay is instantaneous and telemetry never blocks the UI. 
- Sending only on `visit`, `game_start`, and `game_exit` allows computing play time from start/exit timestamps while reducing network noise. 

### Description
- Removed frequent heartbeat and frequent event sends, and stopped sending telemetry on `pause`/`resume`/`page_hide` events; kept `visit`, `game_start`, and `game_exit` sends only using `createTelemetry`'s API. 
- Implemented non-blocking async dispatch: messages are queued via `setTimeout(..., 0)` and delivered with `navigator.sendBeacon` where available, with a fallback to `fetch(..., { mode: 'no-cors', keepalive: true })` and finally an `Image` fallback. 
- Reworked telemetry state: removed heartbeat fields, added `gameStartSentAt`, `sessionExitSent`, and `geo` fields; `collectGeoData` now fills `state.geo` via a callback instead of sending separate geo events. 
- Kept payload fields intact and changed `endSession` to emit `game_exit` with `session_started_at_unix_ms` and `session_ended_at_unix_ms`, and guarded against duplicate exit sends with `sessionExitSent`; `pauseSession`/`resumeSession` now only update timing state.

author: matalve
body:
## Summary

This PR adds repository-level guidance files for AI assistants and pull request workflow consistency.

The goal is to make the project's working conventions travel with the repository instead of depending on one specific IDE, computer, or chat history.

## What changed

- Added `AGENTS.md`
- Added `.github/pull_request_template.md`

## Why

This project now has a fairly specific workflow and collaboration style, including:

- GitHub communication should be in English
- PR descriptions should be written in Markdown
- always update `master` before creating a new branch
- prefer small, iterative PRs
- push after each commit so previews and checks can run
- verify that the latest expected merge is actually present in `master` before starting new work

Without repo-level guidance, those conventions are easy to lose when switching computers, IDEs, or AI tools.

## Files added

### `AGENTS.md`

Documents repo-specific guidance for AI coding assistants, including:

- project/runtime context
- branching and git workflow
- PR expectations
- testing strategy
- Cloudflare-specific guidance
- legacy-file handling
- documentation expectations

### `.github/pull_request_template.md`

Adds a default GitHub PR template with sections for:

- Summary
- What changed
- Why
- Testing
- Notes

## Result

These conventions now live inside the repository and can follow the project across:

- different computers
- different IDEs
- different AI assistants
- future contributors

## Notes

- `AGENTS.md` is primarily for AI/repo workflow guidance
- the GitHub PR template is enforced through GitHub's normal PR creation flow
- both files are intentionally lightweight and can be expanded over time as the workflow evolves

author: miyaoka
body:
## 概要

barrel-import ESLint ルールで、外部からネストされた子 feature を直接参照できてしまうバグを修正。あわせて、`barrelFiles` と `scopes` オプションを追加し、プロジェクト固有のハードコードを除去して汎用的なプラグインとして使えるようにした。

## 背景

`features/feat-A/` から `features/feat-B/features/feat-B-child-A/` をバレル経由で import した場合、現行ルールはこれを許可していた。子 feature は親 feature の内部実装であり、外部からは親のバレル（`features/feat-B/`）経由でのみアクセス可能にすべき。

原因は2つ:
- `extractScope` が最深スコープのみを返す設計で、import 先のルートスコープ（外部から見える境界）を考慮していなかった
- `isBarrelImport` が `index.ts` を無条件で許可しており、明示指定で制限を迂回できた

また、`features` / `shared` のディレクトリ名と依存方向（`shared → features` 禁止）がハードコードされており、将来の独立プラグイン化に障害があった。eslint-plugin-boundaries の設計を調査したが、`type` ベースのフラット定義では再帰的ネスト構造を扱えないため、自作ルールの拡張で対応した。

## 変更内容

### ネストスコープの修正

- `extractAllScopes` を追加し、パス内の全スコープを浅い順に取得できるようにした
- `check` 関数で `toRootScope`（最浅スコープ）を取得し、import 元がルートスコープの内部にいるかどうかで許可するバレルを切り替える
- `isBarrelImport` で拡張子付き import 時も直前のセグメントが許可スコープ名と一致するか検証

### 同名子スコープの区別

- `ScopeInfo` 型を導入し、`scope`（リーフペア）と `fullPath`（パス先頭からスコープ末尾まで）を保持
- 同一スコープ判定を `fullPath` ベースに変更し、異なる親の下にある同名子スコープ（例: `feat-B/features/common` と `feat-D/features/common`）を正しく区別

### `barrelFiles` オプション

- デフォルト: `["index.ts", "index.tsx"]`
- ユーザーが `index.js` / `index.jsx` 等を追加可能
- 拡張子なしのディレクトリ import は `barrelFiles` に関係なく常に許可

### `scopes` オプション

- `features` / `shared` のハードコードを完全に除去
- 各スコープは `directories`（ディレクトリ名リスト）と `dependsOn`（依存可能なスコープ名リスト）を宣言
- `buildScopePattern` で正規表現を動的構築（メタ文字エスケープ付き）
- デフォルト設定は従来と同じ挙動:
  ```json
  {
    "shared": { "directories": ["shared"], "dependsOn": [] },
    "features": { "directories": ["features"], "dependsOn": ["shared"] }
  }
  ```

### 設定バリデーション

- 空 `scopes`、空 `directories`、重複ディレクトリ名、未定義 `dependsOn` を検出しエラー報告

### テスト（46テスト）

- テストパス名を抽象化（`feat-A`, `feat-B`, `feat-B-child-A` 等）
- カスタム scopes（`core` / `common` / `modules` の3層）のテストスイートを追加
- 設定バリデーションのテスト（空 scopes、空 directories、重複、未定義 dependsOn）
- 同名子スコープの回帰テスト
- 欠けていたテストケースを網羅的に追加

## スコープ

- **スコープ内**: ネストスコープのバグ修正、同名子スコープの区別、`barrelFiles` / `scopes` オプション化、設定バリデーション、テスト整理
- **スコープ外（対応しない）**: 既存コードベースでの違反検出。lint を実行すれば検出される

## 確認事項

- [ ] `pnpm --filter @gozd/eslint-plugin test --run` が全テスト通過すること
- [ ] `pnpm lint:all` で既存コードに新たな違反が出ないか確認

author: ritadias
body:
### Description

telemetry consent off: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89c23eb9-a62b-481a-b32b-edc388b97e43


#### What's available

- **Feedback dialog in the help menu**: editors can submit feedback directly from the studio help menu with the source `studio-help-menu`
- **`FeedbackDialog` component**: drop-in UI with sentiment selection, message field, image attachment, and contact consent toggle
- **`useInStudioFeedback` hook**: returns a `sendFeedback` function with all studio context tags pre-filled, for building custom feedback UIs
- **Configurable DSN and source**: both entry points accept a `dsn` and `source` so feedback can target different Sentry projects and be filtered per feature
- **PII stripping**: when telemetry consent is denied: userId are automatically removed before sending. 

Scenario | name/email | userId
-- | -- | --
Telemetry granted | Included | Included
Telemetry denied, contact consent yes | Included | Stripped
Telemetry denied, contact consent no | Stripped | Stripped

- **Hidden in dashboard**: the feedback menu item does not appear when the studio is embedded in the Sanity Dashboard
- **Feedback routes through a tunnel** at `api.sanity.io/vX/intake/feedback` to avoid direct Sentry requests and adblock blocking
 - **Added a tunnel for error reporting**: errors now route through `api.sanity.io/vX/intake/tracing`, matching the feedback tunnel approach. **A follow-up for aligning telemetry denial and consent behaviour with the error tunnel will be done separately**

> [!Note]
> The current implementation is tightly coupled to studio context providers (workspace, router, current user, telemetry). This is the intended scope for now. Decoupling it for use in other products (e.g., Manage) will be handled in a separate effort.

#### Good to know

- **`feedbackVersion` is required**: tracks tag schema changes over time so BigQuery queries can differentiate between versions
- **`message` is mandatory for Sentry**: if your UI allows sentiment-only submissions, provide a fallback (the built-in dialog already does this)
- **Dialog-specific fields are optional on `sendFeedback`**: `sentiment`, `contactConsent`, and `attachments` are only needed if custom UI collects them

### What to review

> Why not use the same client as the error?
- Different tunnels: feedback uses /intake/feedback, errors use /intake/tracing
- Different transports: errors buffer until telemetry consent resolves (to be changed in a follow up PR, but important context for now). Feedback sends immediately and strips PII at event construction
- Error client may not exist: initialization guards can prevent it from being created; feedback must always work
- Feedback supports multiple DSNs: the error client is locked to STUDIO_DSN

> Why not use beforeSend for the feedback to strip PII? 
- PII never enters the event: fields are conditionally omitted when building the event, rather than added then stripped
- No extra indirection: the logic is visible where the event is constructed, not hidden in a separate callback

### Testing

- You can manually test it by opening the help menu and selecting the "Send feedback" button
- You can then go to slack and open the channel #studio-feedback-sentry where you will see a snippet of it with a link to sentry
- Clicking the sentry link on the slack message, you will see all details attached that make sense to have in the event.

- Unit tests have been added where I felt they made sense 

### Notes for release

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/992d8156-30dd-47b2-ad79-541435d3e7f7


You can now provide Sanity feedback directly from your studio by opening the "Help and Resources" menu and picking send feedback!

author: anpicci
body:
## Summary

- Rewrite `README.md` into a true landing page and move detailed workflow/reference material behind the docs hub.
- Promote `docs/index.md` to the canonical docs map with clearer newcomer, workflow, troubleshooting, architecture, developer, and archival sections.
- Surface previously under-linked but important docs such as `environment_packaging.md`, `ddr_outputs_and_pkl.md`, and `workflow_module_chain.md`.
- Clarify and preserve the split roles of the workflow/config cluster instead of merging pages:
  - `workflow_and_yaml_hub.md`
  - `quickstart_run2.md`
  - `how_to_run_analysis_workflow.md`
  - `run_analysis_configuration.md`
- Demote legacy/historical material more explicitly so it no longer competes with the primary onboarding path.

## Motivation

Before this PR, `topeft` had a strong documentation set, but the top-level navigation still created unnecessary friction:

- `README.md` competed with the docs hub by duplicating scenario/configuration/reference material.
- There were too many plausible “start here” pages, which made the newcomer path ambiguous.
- Some useful operational or architecture pages were under-linked and easy to miss.
- Legacy and archival material was still prominent enough to blur the active workflow path.
- The workflow/config pages overlapped in purpose unless the reader already knew which one they wanted.

This PR addresses those issues by making the routing clearer without changing workflow semantics and without collapsing pages that still serve distinct roles.

## Implementation details

### A. Turn `README.md` into a landing page

The README was heavily reduced so it now behaves as a landing page rather than a second workflow manual.

Main changes:
- keep repo identity and relation to `topcoffea`
- define a primary newcomer sequence
- add a “choose your next guide” section by intent
- point readers to `docs/index.md` as the authoritative docs map
- replace long in-README scenario/config/reference/historical material with links

Large duplicated sections were removed, including:
- metadata/scenario explanation that is better owned by dedicated docs
- detailed configuration guidance
- large historical reproduction content in the primary landing flow

This reduces drift risk and makes the docs authority clearer.

### B. Strengthen `docs/index.md` as the canonical hub

`docs/index.md` was restructured into a stronger canonical map.

Key changes:
- clearer `Start here` sequence
- stronger `Workflow guides and reference` section
- dedicated `Troubleshooting and validation` section
- dedicated `Architecture` section
- cleaner `Legacy / archival` section
- explicit note that legacy pages are archival and not the default onboarding path
- removal of duplicated placement of `run2_legacy_notes.md`

This page now answers:
- where a newcomer should start
- which page is authoritative for a given topic
- which pages are current vs archival
- which pages are operator-facing vs maintainer-facing

### C. Surface under-linked docs

Three lightly linked but important pages were surfaced more clearly:

- `docs/environment_packaging.md`
  - linked directly from `docs/taskvine_workflow.md`
  - also surfaced from `README.md` / `docs/index.md`

- `docs/ddr_outputs_and_pkl.md`
  - linked from `docs/quickstart_run2.md`
  - surfaced in troubleshooting/validation routing

- `docs/workflow_module_chain.md`
  - linked from `docs/analysis_processing.md`
  - surfaced in architecture/maintainer routing

This improves discoverability without changing page ownership.

### D. Keep the workflow/config cluster split, but clarify page roles

A deliberate choice in this PR is to **not** merge the main workflow/config docs cluster.

Instead, their openings and “next step” language were tightened so each page has a clearer canonical role:

#### `docs/workflow_and_yaml_hub.md`
Role:
- orientation and decision hub

What changed:
- makes clear that readers should start here to understand the model
- explicitly routes readers to exactly one next guide
- warns against starting with legacy quickstarts

#### `docs/quickstart_run2.md`
Role:
- first successful run guide

What changed:
- opening clarifies this is the first-run path, not the full operator/config manual
- “Next steps” section now points clearly to TaskVine, wrapper, or config pages
- output-schema note now links to `ddr_outputs_and_pkl.md`

#### `docs/how_to_run_analysis_workflow.md`
Role:
- wrapper/operator recipe

What changed:
- opening explicitly says this is for readers who already know they want the wrapper entrypoint
- clarifies it is not the primary newcomer page and not the detailed config manual
- adds direct handoff to `run_analysis_configuration.md`

#### `docs/run_analysis_configuration.md`
Role:
- detailed configuration and troubleshooting guide

What changed:
- opening explicitly positions it as the deep config/troubleshooting page
- routes first-time readers back to the hub/quickstart
- routes wrapper-specific readers to `how_to_run_analysis_workflow.md`

This keeps the current structure but makes the separation intelligible to a new reader.

### E. Clarify `taskvine_workflow.md` and keep it as a branch, not a rival entrypoint

`docs/taskvine_workflow.md` was adjusted so it no longer reads like a competing full-workflow manual.

Changes:
- opening explicitly says it is the distributed-execution branch of the main onboarding path
- routes readers back to hub/quickstart if they are starting from scratch
- adds a handoff to `run_analysis_configuration.md` for deeper tuning/troubleshooting
- links to `environment_packaging.md` for detailed packaging policy

This preserves TaskVine-specific detail while reducing entrypoint competition.

### F. Demote archival material more explicitly

The docs now more clearly separate active workflow guidance from historical material.

Examples:
- legacy pages were grouped more clearly in `docs/index.md`
- archival wording was strengthened
- README no longer carries long historical reproduction material in the default newcomer path

Importantly, legacy pages were **not deleted**. They were retained but demoted.

### G. Semantics intentionally unchanged

This PR is docs-only.

It does **not** change:
- analysis behavior
- metadata/scenario logic
- TaskVine policy
- workflow execution semantics
- plotting/data-card production logic
- developer/test behavior

The change is about navigation, page roles, and documentation authority only.

## Testing

This PR was verified as a docs-only change.

What was run:
- mandatory preflight:
  - `git status -sb`
  - `git diff --name-status`
  - `git clean -nd`
- targeted `rg` sanity checks for routing terms, page-role language, and expected links
- `git diff` inspection before commit
- `git show --stat`
- `git show --name-only`
- full `git show`
- final `git status -sb`

Limitations:
- no `compileall`
- no `pytest`

That was intentional because the PR only changes documentation text and navigation structure.

## Review notes

- The most important review point is the **intended role split** of the workflow/config cluster. This PR intentionally keeps those pages separate:
  - hub = orientation / decision page
  - quickstart = first successful run
  - wrapper page = operator recipe
  - config page = detailed tuning and troubleshooting
- Reviewers should check that `README.md` now behaves like a landing page and does not drift back into a second manual.
- Reviewers should also check that legacy pages are still available for provenance/history, but no longer compete with the main onboarding path.
- No workflow or analysis semantics are intended to change.

author: mnemonice
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/MnemOnicE/credon-core/security/code-scanning/4](https://github.com/MnemOnicE/credon-core/security/code-scanning/4)

In general, fix this by explicitly defining a minimal `permissions` block for the workflow or for the specific job, granting only the scopes needed (typically `contents: read` for a basic CI/analysis workflow). This prevents the job from inheriting broader repository defaults and documents the intended permissions.

For this specific workflow, the simplest and safest fix without changing current behavior is to add a `permissions` block at the workflow root (so it applies to all jobs) immediately after the `name:` declaration (line 1) and before the `on:` block (line 3). Since the job only checks out code and runs the SonarCloud action, `contents: read` is sufficient in most setups. If later you discover that additional scopes are needed (for example, to comment on PRs), they can be added explicitly, but the minimal recommended starting point from CodeQL is `contents: read`. No additional imports, methods, or definitions are required; this is purely a YAML configuration change in `.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml`.

author: dishangyijiao
body:
## Problem

When the worker starts up and resets stale jobs, the reset event is logged twice in the application logs:

1. Once inside `_reset_stale_jobs()` (line 334 in `worker.py`):
   ```
   Reset 2 stale job(s) to 'queued'
   ```
2. Once in `run_worker()` (line 348 in `worker.py`):
   ```
   Reset 2 stale job(s) from 'running' to 'queued'
   ```

This creates confusing noise in the logs — operators see two near-identical messages for the same event.

## Root Cause

When `_reset_stale_jobs` was refactored to include its own logging (commit `1981c0c`), the existing `print()`-based log in `run_worker` was updated to use `_worker_log.info` instead of being removed. Since `_reset_stale_jobs` already logs the event, the log in `run_worker` became redundant.

## Fix

Remove the three lines in `run_worker` that capture the return value and re-log it. The `_reset_stale_jobs` function's internal log is the canonical location for this event.

```diff
-        reset_count = _reset_stale_jobs(conn)
-        if reset_count > 0:
-            _worker_log.info("Reset %d stale job(s) from 'running' to 'queued'", reset_count)
+        _reset_stale_jobs(conn)
```

## Verification

Manual review: `_reset_stale_jobs` already logs at line 334:
```python
if count > 0:
    _worker_log.info("Reset %d stale job(s) to 'queued'", count)
```

Existing tests (`test_worker.py::TestResetStaleJobs`) test `_reset_stale_jobs` directly and are unaffected by this change. No test captures log output from `run_worker`.

## Risks

None — this is a pure log-line removal. No logic, no DB operations, no user-visible behavior changes.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **3.0.4** to **7.3.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   -------------------

**License:**

- **0BSD license** — the project license has been changed from MIT to
  `0BSD <https://opensource.org/license/0bsd>`_, a maximally permissive
  license with no attribution requirement. All prior 7.x releases
  should also be considered 0BSD licensed as of this release.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**Features:**

- Added ``mime_type`` field to detection results — identifies file types
  for both binary (via magic number matching) and text content. Returned
  in all ``detect()``, ``detect_all()``, and ``UniversalDetector`` results.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)
- New ``pipeline/magic.py`` module detects 40+ binary file formats
  including images, audio/video, archives, documents, executables, and
  fonts. ZIP-based formats (XLSX, DOCX, JAR, APK, EPUB, wheel,
  OpenDocument) are distinguished by entry filenames.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Fixed incorrect equivalence between UTF-16-LE and UTF-16-BE in
  accuracy testing — these are distinct encodings with different byte
  order, not interchangeable
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**Performance:**

- Added 4 new modules to mypyc compilation (orchestrator, confusion,
  magic, ascii), bringing the total to 11 compiled modules
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Capped statistical scoring at 16 KB — bigram models converge quickly,
  so large files no longer score the full 200 KB. Worst-case detection
  time dropped from 62ms to 26ms with no accuracy loss.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Replaced ``dataclasses.replace()`` with direct ``DetectionResult``
  construction on hot paths, eliminating ~354k function calls per full
  test suite run
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**Build:**

- Added riscv64 to the mypyc wheel build matrix — prebuilt wheels are
  now published for RISC-V Linux alongside existing architectures
  (`Bruno Verachten <https://github.com/gounthar>`_,
  `348 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/348>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added ``include_encodings`` and ``exclude_encodings`` parameters to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — restrict or exclude specific
  encodings from the candidate set, with corresponding
  ``-i``/``--include-encodings`` and ``-x``/``--exclude-encodings``
  CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``no_match_encoding`` (default ``"cp1252"``) and
  ``empty_input_encoding`` (default ``"utf-8"``) parameters — control
  which encoding is returned when no candidate survives the pipeline or
  the input is empty, with corresponding CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``-l``/``--language`` flag to ``chardetect`` CLI — shows the
  detected language (ISO 639-1 code and English name) alongside the encoding
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `342 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/342>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added PEP 263 encoding declaration detection — `` -*- coding: ... -*-``
  and `` coding=...`` declarations on lines 1–2 of Python source files are
  now recognized with confidence 0.95
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `249 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/249>`_)
- Added ``chardet.universaldetector`` backward-compatibility stub so that
  ``from chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector`` works with a
  deprecation warning
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `341 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/341>`_)

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of ASCII text containing ``++`` or ``+word``
  patterns
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `332 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/332>`_,
  `335 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/335>`_)
- Fixed 0.5s startup cost on first ``detect()`` call — model norms are now
  computed during loading instead of lazily iterating 21M entries
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `333 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/333>`_,
  `336 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/336>`_)
- Fixed undocumented encoding name changes between chardet 5.x and 7.0 —
  ``detect()`` now returns chardet 5.x-compatible names by default
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `338 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/338>`_)
- Improved ISO-2022-JP family detection — recognizes ESC sequences for
  ISO-2022-JP-2004 (JIS X 0213) and ISO-2022-JP-EXT (JIS X 0201 Kana)
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Fixed silent truncation of corrupt model data (``iter_unpack`` yielded
  fewer tuples instead of raising)
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Fixed incorrect date in LICENSE
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**Performance:**

- 5.5x faster first-detect time (~0.42s → ~0.075s) by computing model
  norms as a side-product of ``load_models()``
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- ~40% faster model parsing via ``struct.iter_unpack`` for bulk entry
  extraction (eliminates ~305K individual ``unpack`` calls)
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**New API parameters:**

- Added ``compat_names`` parameter (default ``True``) to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — set to ``False`` to get raw Python
  codec names instead of chardet 5.x/6.x compatible display names
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Added ``prefer_superset`` parameter (default ``False``) — remaps legacy
  ISO/subset encodings to their modern Windows/CP superset equivalents
  (e.g., ASCII → Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 → Windows-1252).
  **This will default to ``True`` in the next major version (8.0).**
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Deprecated ``should_rename_legacy`` in favor of ``prefer_superset`` —
  a deprecation warning is emitted when used
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**Improvements:**

- Switched internal canonical encoding names to Python codec names
  (e.g., ``"utf-8"`` instead of ``"UTF-8"``), with ``compat_names``
  controlling the public output format.  See :doc:`usage` for the full
  mapping table.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Added ``lookup_encoding()`` to ``registry`` for case-insensitive
  resolution of arbitrary encoding name input to canonical names
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Achieved 100% line coverage across all source modules (+31 tests)
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Updated benchmark numbers: 98.2% encoding accuracy, 95.2% language
  accuracy on 2,510 test files
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
- Pinned test-data cloning to chardet release version tags for
  reproducible builds
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.0.1
   ```
   -------------------

## Summary

Fixes #5719 .

<!--------------------------------------------------------------------------
👉 STEP 4:  In a few sentences, write a summary explaining:

     From the perspective of an end user, what problem are you solving?
     What did you change?

     You can add the magic phrase "Fixes #1234" to automatically close
     issue #1234 when your PR is merged.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------->

## Details

glob@7 with leading dot-slash pattern won't return the same path files.
But, glob@8 with leading dot-slash pattern will return a file path prefixed with "./".
Than, we will got two file paths reference to the same file.
This will cause `EEXIST: file already exists` error when running with `COPYFILE_EXCL` mode.

This PR uses `path.normalize` to dedup the file paths.

## How it was tested

1. Added a unit test.
2. Tested in the repo where the issue happened.

author: copilot
body:
The previous UI was split between a darwinkit/AppKit menu-bar-only agent (macOS, no Dock icon) and a raw CLI (everything else). No GUI on Windows or Linux; no Dock icon anywhere.

## Changes

### Single cross-platform UI — `cmd/nexvault/ui/app.go`
Replaces `app_darwin.go` + `app_cli.go` with a single no-build-tag file using **Fyne v2.7.3**. Platform rendering:

| OS | Backend | App presence |
|---|---|---|
| macOS (Silicon + Intel) | Metal | Dock icon |
| Windows 10 / 11 | DirectX/ANGLE | Taskbar |
| Linux | OpenGL | Panel + tray |

`Run()` dispatches to CLI when a known sub-command is passed, otherwise opens the GUI — same binary, both modes:

```bash
nexvault                          # → opens Fyne window with Dock icon
nexvault list -vault ~/secure     # → CLI output, no window
```

### GUI layout
- Toolbar: **New Vault** · **Open Vault** · **Lock** · **Decrypt…** · **Delete** · **Refresh**
- Entry table with columns: Vault Path / Size / Added
- Folder-picker dialogs for vault and drop directories; masked password fields
- Status bar showing lock state, vault path, watch path
- System tray icon (all platforms) for Lock / Show / Quit without opening the window

### Dependency changes (`go.mod`)
- `fyne.io/fyne/v2 v2.7.3` → direct dependency
- `github.com/progrium/darwinkit` → removed

### `internal/watcher/watcher.go`
Fixed spelling: `relativise` → `relativize`.

### `README.md`
Rewritten: platform support table, per-OS build instructions, GUI walkthrough, CLI reference, updated security design and dependency table.

### Motivation
- Add three operational KPIs to the Dashboard Overview so users can see (1) pending units to receive (value + units), (2) pending units to ship with a split between with-stock and without-stock (value + units), and (3) year-to-date sales in euros, using existing `Stock` and `Sales Data` sheets.

### Description
- Add `stock_filtered` and align it with the global brand filter by restricting stock rows to articles present in the filtered `ventas` when applicable. 
- Build a `unit_cost_map` from `ventas['Precio Coste']` (grouped by `Artículo` with numeric casting and safe fallbacks) and map it into stock rows. 
- Compute: pending-to-receive units and value from `Total Pendiente Recibir * Precio Coste`, pending-to-ship units and value from `Reservas * Precio Coste`, and split pending-to-ship into `Reservas Con Stock` and `Reservas Sin Stock` where `Reservas Sin Stock = max(Reservas - Stock, 0)`, and calculate their respective values. 
- Compute current-year accumulated sales as the sum of `Importe Neto` for `Año Factura == manager.current_year`, add all metrics to the `stats` dict, and render them in a new “Indicadores operativos” KPI row (showing euros and unit captions); include numeric casting and safe defaults when columns are missing.
