DAG do Airflow (spacex_etl_dag.py)
Configuração completa do pipeline de ingestão e dbt utilizando DockerOperator.
Ajuste de paths e mounts do projeto dbt (/usr/app).
Variáveis de ambiente padronizadas e consistentes com Docker Compose.
dbt
profiles.yml configurado para PostgreSQL via Docker (db_postgres).
Dockerfile dbt corrigido, com ENTRYPOINT removido e dbt deps executado durante build.
Packages e dependências definidas no packages.yml.
Docker Compose
Criação de volumes persistentes para Postgres e Metabase.
Serviços isolados: airflow-webserver, airflow-scheduler, airflow-init, dbt, ingestion-engine, db_postgres e metabase.
Configuração de rede dedicada (spacex_etl_pipeline_default) para todos os containers.
Healthchecks, variáveis de ambiente e dependências entre serviços ajustadas.
Objetivo final
Permitir que o pipeline seja executado 100% via Docker em qualquer máquina com Docker/Docker Compose, garantindo portabilidade e consistência.

Extracts VariableTypeFilter.inferValueType into a static helper that accepts an ObjectMapper, so it can be reused by other filters.

Adds VariableTypeScopeFilter, which:

- Infers the JSON type of variable values and applies separate allowed-type sets depending on whether the variable is local (scopeKey != processInstanceKey) or root (scopeKey == processInstanceKey).
- Supports independent inclusion/exclusion configuration per scope and derives immutable allowed-type sets.
- Accepts all non-variable records and only filters VariableRecordValue instances.
- Is guarded by a minimum broker version 8.10.0, where the required scope information is available.

Adds unit tests for VariableTypeScopeFilter to cover:

- Local vs root scope behavior.
- Inclusion-only, exclusion-only, and mixed configurations.
- Fallback behavior when no rules are configured for a given scope.

This is a building block for downstream components (e.g., Optimize) to configure scope-aware variable export based on inferred variable types.

## Related issues

Closes: https://github.com/camunda/camunda/issues/48103
Relates to https://github.com/camunda/camunda/issues/46267 (pdp-3435 – scope-aware variable export configuration for Optimize)

## Summary

- Adds `--max-fee-per-gas` and `--max-priority-fee` flags (in gwei) to all transaction commands: deploy, upgrade, start, stop, terminate
- Also available as env vars: `ECLOUD_MAX_FEE_PER_GAS`, `ECLOUD_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE`
- When omitted, existing gas estimation behavior is unchanged
- When provided, overrides the estimated values and recalculates the displayed cost

**Context:** 10 transactions timed out on mainnet today due to gas estimation being too low for current network conditions. The SDK's 100% buffer on batch transactions wasn't enough. This gives operators an escape hatch.

```bash
# Override max fee to 80 gwei
ecloud compute app deploy --max-fee-per-gas 80

# Override both
ecloud compute app start <app-id> --max-fee-per-gas 100 --max-priority-fee 10

# Via env vars
ECLOUD_MAX_FEE_PER_GAS=80 ecloud compute app deploy
```

- [ ] Deploy without flags — verify behavior unchanged

author: zzzeek
body:
the password written into mysql_pw_cache.cnf needs to be written there with quotes to accommodate a small set of special characters,
namely the pound sign #.   For other special characters, including
single and double quotes as well as the backslash, these characters
are now disallowed by mariadbaccount_controller.go, along with most
other non-alphanumeric characters
outside of a specific whitelist; this rule applies to all MariaDBAccount
CRs.   the MariaDBPassword for root is rendered into many shell script
commands with various styles of quoting, as well as rendered into
a MySQL ALTER USER command; maintaining a whitelist is the safest
and clearest way to steer clear of a variety of non alphanumeric
characters that may be entered by users who are manually creating
secrets.

Ideally, auto-password generation will be used for the DB root password in the same way as is used for other database clients, which uses alphanumeric only for passwords.

References: [OSPRH-28209](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OSPRH-28209)

body: Replace the single GetObject stream in S3.Open with parallel range-GET requests for objects larger than 32 MiB. 8 workers download chunks concurrently and reassemble them in order via io.Pipe, multiplying S3 throughput for cold snapshot downloads (observed ~100 MB/s single-stream → 400+ MB/s with parallel connections on staging hardware).

author: rabbitlair
body:
Closes #1172 

Raises the default PHPStan level from 1 to 6 per the [Lullabot ADR](https://architecture.lullabot.com/adr/20260320-use-phpstan/).

Projects with pre-existing violations can opt into a baseline to suppress them, so CI only fails on new code:                               
```
task test:phpstan:generate-baseline
git add phpstan.neon phpstan-baseline.neon
git commit -m "Add PHPStan level 6 baseline"
```

This generates `phpstan-baseline.neon` and creates `phpstan.neon` wiring it in alongside `phpstan.neon.dist`. Projects without a baseline will run at level 6 immediately on upgrade.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a production-grade execution layer (Agent Runtime Fabric) that exposes a strict tool gateway for BYOK orchestration and ledgering.
- Support two explicit toolsets: deployment/app-runtime tooling and a safe coding/file toolset without exposing raw shell access.
- Offer disposable session workspaces, process lifecycle management, sandboxed code execution, and persistent logs/artifacts.

### Description

- Introduce a FastAPI-based runtime gateway (`backend/app.py`) with endpoints for session lifecycle, deployment/runtime tools, and safe coding/file tools, plus CORS and request logging to a persistence store. 
- Add typed request/response models and runtime policy definitions in `backend/models.py` and `backend/policy.py` to centralize contracts and policy limits.
- Implement `RuntimeManager` (`backend/runtime_manager.py`) to manage sessions, workspace zones, cloning/checking out repos, installing deps, starting/stopping processes, running snippets, searching files, function mapping, bracket tracking, and log streaming.
- Add a simple persistence layer (`backend/storage.py`) to append tool logs, read the ledger, and write recorded package manifests, and wire it into the app for tool-usage ledgering.
- Provide a lightweight frontend cockpit (`frontend/*`) with an HTML UI, JavaScript client (`app.js`) and CSS for interacting with the runtime gateway and exercising both toolsets.
- Add a small `run_server.py` wrapper to start uvicorn in constrained environments (option to disable signal handlers), plus `requirements.txt` and `.gitignore` for the backend.

### Testing

author: chance-wnb
body:
## Summary

This change removes the floating `main`\-branch marketplace install behavior and pins plugin installs to a specific release ref instead.

The installer and marketplace manifest now use the release tag for the current package version, which gives us a version boundary for new installs and avoids automatically picking up whatever is on the default branch.

## What Changed

- Updated the Claude marketplace registration flow to use `wandb/claude_code_weave_plugin`.
- Updated `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to pin the plugin source to `sha` and `ref` keys.
- Kept `weave-claude-plugin install` re-validating marketplace and plugin registration for existing installs, so older floating installs can be repaired by rerunning install
- Documented the release requirement in the README

## Security Impact

Previously, marketplace installs pulled directly from the repository default branch, so any compromised or unintended push could affect all future installs immediately.

With this change:

- installs are pinned to an explicit release tag and sha
- users get a version boundary between released builds
- the project can enforce tighter release controls with protected tags

## Operational Notes

Releases must create and push the matching protected tag before publishing, for example:

```bash
git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0
```

Recommended controls:

- restrict who can create or update release tags
- protect release tags in GitHub
- treat release tags as immutable
- add CI or release checks to ensure the expected `v<package-version>` tag exists before publishing

## Verification

- `npm run build` passes
- `weave-claude-plugin install` succeeds when the matching release tag exists

Sets up the full project scaffold based on the finalized Skybox architecture. Nothing is fully implemented yet — this is the skeleton everything else will be built on.

## Structure

- **`backend/`** — FastAPI app with async SQLAlchemy, APScheduler, and watchdog
  - `models/` — VideoFile, Load, Assignment, SyncJob

- **`docker-compose.yml`** — 2 services, ARM64-compatible, named volume for SQLite, bind-mounts for video storage and SD card path
- **`.env.example`** — documents all env vars with tier 1/2/3 scraper comments

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build
```

- Frontend: http://localhost

body:
Me, yet again! I swear I have a life Taylor.

In https://github.com/laravel/framework/pull/59298 we added `releaseOnTerminationSignals` to events. 

But, I forgot to route it through groups, groups basically merge their attributes onto each event.. from reading it so this PR this means you can opt out properly now.

```php
// You could not opt out before...
Schedule::daily()                                                                                                                          
      ->withoutOverlapping(1440, releaseOnTerminationSignals: false)  
      ->group(function (Schedule $schedule) {                                                                                                
          $schedule->command('emails:send');                                                                                                 
          $schedule->command('emails:cleanup');                                                                                              
      });           
```

- Reject chunked request bodies for sensitive methods to avoid edge-case proxy/handler issues with streaming `DELETE`/`OPTIONS`. 
- Hardening the server action used by the sign-in button by verifying request origin/referer before performing server-side sign-in operations. 

### Description

- Added ASF and ZIP local-file-header magic checks in `InstructorAttachmentService` and reject ASF-like uploads immediately while treating raw ZIP local headers as `application/zip` for downstream Office validation. 
- Kept ZIP handling that restricts ZIP uploads to Office Open XML extensions and confirmed Office XML structure via an existing `hasOfficeXmlStructure` check. 
- Added `enforceNoChunkedDeleteOrOptions` to the BFF route to block requests using `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` for `DELETE` and `OPTIONS`, and exported an `OPTIONS` handler to the route. 
- Secured `SignInButton` server action by reading `origin`/`referer` from `headers()` and aborting the action unless the request origin matches `envServer.HSS_WEB_ORIGIN`. 
- Bumped `next` and `eslint-config-next` in `apps/web/package.json`, adjusted pnpm overrides for `minio>fast-xml-parser` and `hono`, and removed `Pygments` from `requirements.txt`.

author: ddasgupta4
body:
## Problem

Two separate data-loss bugs found while dogfooding v0.76.3.

> **AI assistance disclosure:** This PR was authored with AI assistance (George / Claude Opus 4 via OpenClaw), operating on a live v0.76.3 install with 3970 memories and 112 summary_jobs. Bugs were identified by direct database inspection and source code analysis. Fix approach reviewed and approved by the human operator before submission.

---

### Bug 1: `summary_jobs` permanently stuck in `processing` after daemon crash

**Impact:** Every daemon restart abandons in-flight summary jobs. The worker only polls `status = 'pending'` — anything left in `'processing'` is silently lost forever.

Observed: 58 of 112 summary_jobs stuck in processing on a live install after normal use.

**Root cause:** `startSummaryWorker()` starts polling with no crash recovery step. The per-job error handler (within a single run) works correctly, but nothing runs at startup to clean up jobs from a previous crashed process.

**Fix:** Add startup crash recovery at the top of `startSummaryWorker()` — single write tx, non-fatal if it fails — that resets `'processing'` → `'pending'` (or `'dead'` if `attempts >= max_attempts`).

---

### Bug 2: `embed backfill` / embedding tracker cycles infinitely on duplicate-hash memories

**Impact:** Two memory rows with identical content create a permanent "missing embeddings" loop. `signet embed audit` always reports N missing regardless of how many times backfill runs.

Observed: 75 memories permanently reported as missing; `signet embed backfill` reports `re-embedded 50 of 50 (75 still missing)` on every run with no convergence.

**Root cause:** `embeddings` has a `UNIQUE(content_hash)` constraint. The backfill write uses `ON CONFLICT(content_hash) DO UPDATE SET source_id = excluded.source_id`. When two memories share a hash:
1. Embed A → `{hash=H, source_id=A}`
2. Embed B → conflict reassigns `source_id` to B
3. A has no `source_id` match → shows as missing again
4. Repeat forever

Both the audit (`getEmbeddingGapStats`) and backfill SELECT queries join on `source_id = m.id` only, so they never see the hash-attributed embedding that covers the other memory.

**Fix:** Change the `LEFT JOIN` in `getEmbeddingGapStats`, `reembedMissingMemoriesBatch`, and the embedding tracker's stale-row query to also match on `e.content_hash = m.content_hash`. A memory is "embedded" if either its `source_id` is directly referenced OR an embedding with the same content hash exists. The vector is identical for duplicate content so this is semantically correct.

---

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/daemon/src/pipeline/summary-worker.ts` | Startup crash recovery: reset `processing` → `pending`/`dead`; use `countChanges()` helper and explicit type cast per TS conventions |
| `packages/daemon/src/repair-actions.ts` | Fix JOIN in `getEmbeddingGapStats` and `reembedMissingMemoriesBatch` |
| `packages/daemon/src/embedding-tracker.ts` | Fix JOIN in background tracker stale-row query |
| `packages/daemon/src/repair-actions.test.ts` | Add regression test for duplicate-hash backfill cycle; import `getEmbeddingGapStats` |

---

## Readiness Checklist

- [x] Spec alignment validated (`INDEX.md` + `dependencies.yaml`)
- [x] Agent scoping verified on all new/changed data queries
- [x] Input/config validation and bounds checks added
- [x] Error handling and fallback paths tested (no silent swallow)
- [x] Security checks applied to admin/mutation endpoints
- [x] Docs updated for API/spec/status changes
- [x] Regression tests added for each bug fix
- [x] Lint/typecheck/tests pass locally

> **Note on local checks:** `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint` were not run in the contributing environment (no bun install available). TypeScript conventions from CONTRIBUTING.md were followed manually: `countChanges()` helper used instead of direct property access, explicit type casts on `db.get()` results, no non-null assertions, proper error narrowing in catch blocks. Please flag any violations in review.

body:
Closes #145

---

Closses #145 
fix: replace any types with proper interfaces in subscription-service…

Summary

This PR improves type safety and security in the subscription service by removing all any types and enforcing strict input validation for update operations.

Previously, the updateSubscription method accepted an any input and directly spread it into the database update query. This created a potential security risk in which unintended or malicious fields (e.g., user_id, status) could be injected and persisted.

Changes Made
Introduced strongly typed interfaces (Subscription and UpdateSubscriptionInput) in /types/subscription.ts
Replaced all any types in subscription-service.ts with explicit, well-defined types
Refactored the update logic to use an explicit field allowlist instead of spreading input
Ensured only permitted fields can be updated by the user
Added proper return types to all public methods

Impact
Eliminates risk of field injection attacks during update operations
Improves overall type safety and maintainability
Aligns the service with TypeScript best practices
Ensures ESLint @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any rule passes

Acceptance Criteria
No usage of any in subscription-service.ts
All method signatures are fully typed
Update operations strictly use an allowlist approach
Linting rules pass successfully

author: ueshin
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR updates pandas-on-Spark `Series.map` for the pandas 3 case when the mapper is an empty plain `dict`.

In pandas 3, `pandas.Series.map({})` returns an all-`NaN` `float64` Series. pandas-on-Spark was preserving the input Spark string type for this path, so a string Series produced a pandas `StringDtype` result instead. This PR adds a pandas-3-only branch in `pyspark.pandas.Series.map` so `Series.map({})` returns a null `DoubleType` column for an empty plain dict, which materializes as the same all-`NaN` `float64` result as pandas.

The related test was updated to check the pandas 3 expectation directly, while keeping the pre-pandas-3 expectation unchanged. The existing `defaultdict` coverage remains in place so dict subclasses with `__missing__` continue to follow the existing behavior. This patch also includes a small test adjustment so the local helper used in `test_map` only uppercases string inputs.

### Why are the changes needed?

Without this change, pandas-on-Spark diverges from pandas 3 for `Series.map({})`. For example, a string Series currently returns a pandas `StringDtype` result in pandas-on-Spark, while pandas returns an all-`NaN` `float64` Series.

Aligning this narrow case avoids a pandas-version-specific mismatch in pandas-on-Spark behavior and keeps the test expectation consistent with pandas 3 internals.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, it will behave more like pandas 3.

### How was this patch tested?

Updated the related tests.

author: fw-bot
body:
\* = test_website_modules ### Issue: When accessing a record from the website without logging in, a `404` error occurs if a public record rule filters records by website related domain, for example `[('website_id', '=', website.id)]`. ### Steps to reproduce: - Install the 'website_blog' module and create at least one website. - Enable debug mode. - Go to Settings > Technical > Database Structure > Models. - Open the `blog.post` model. - Go to the 'Record Rules' tab. - For the record 'Blog Post: public: published only', change the domain from `[('website_published', '=', True)]` to `[('website_id', '=', website.id)]`. - Go to Website > Configuration > Blogs. - Open a blog (e.g., Travel). - Select 'My Website' in its 'Website' field. - Open 'My Website' without logging in. - Click on the 'Blog' menu and the blog listing will appear correctly. - Try opening a blog post and a `404` error occurs. ### Reason: 
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Request Lifecycle                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                         │
│  User Request (not logged in)                           │
│       ↓                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐               │
│  │ 1. _pre_dispatch                     │               │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    check_access_rule                 │               │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    _eval_context (compute domain)    │               │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    get_request_website()             │               │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    request.website = None            │  ← Issue      │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    Domain evaluation FAILS           │               │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    Access DENIED → 404 Error         │               │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘               │
│       ↓                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐               │
│  │ 2. _frontend_pre_dispatch            │               │
│  │    (NEVER REACHED)                   │               │
│  │    ↓                                 │               │
│  │    request.website initialized ✓     │  ← Too Late   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘               │
│                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Because `request.website` is initialized later in `_frontend_pre_dispatch`, access rules evaluated earlier in `_pre_dispatch` cannot rely on website context. As a result, record rules depending on `website_id` are evaluated before `request.website` is available, incorrectly denying access to public records. ### Fix: Avoid totally relying on `get_request_website` during access rule evaluation. Use the `request.is_frontend` attribute as a fallback, which is set earlier, to detect frontend requests and ensure correct access handling. task-[4758311](https://www.odoo.com/odoo/project/974/tasks/4758311) --- I confirm I have signed the CLA and read the PR guidelines at www.odoo.com/submit-pr Forward-Port-Of: odoo/odoo#213143

author: acartag7
body:
## Summary

- Railway deploy failed: migration `003` tries to create `UNIQUE (tenant_id, call_id)` on the `events` table, but Postgres rejects this because the table is `PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)` — unique constraints must include all partition key columns
- Migration `001` already documents this: *"The unique constraint MUST include created_at (partition key) per Postgres rules"*
- Fix: make `003` dialect-aware — no-op on Postgres (partitioned), apply narrower constraint only on SQLite (tests)

## Root cause

Migration `003` was written and tested against SQLite (test suite) where there's no partitioning. It was never tested against the production Postgres schema.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (backend tests use SQLite — narrower constraint applied)
- [ ] Merge → Railway auto-deploys → migration `003` runs as no-op on Postgres → healthcheck passes

author: hinriksnaer
body:
## Motivation

The `base_search.py` file is both very frequently modified and getting bigger and bigger by the day. This is a first set of changes intended to both standardize some of the steps and attempt to make things more isolated and decoupled.

for this first one, all search algorithms need to compile and benchmark configs, but they entered the pipeline through different methods (parallel_benchmark, parallel_benchmark_population, parallel_benchmark_flat). There was no single public entry point, and metrics were updated as side effects inside benchmark_function, making it hard to reason about where state changes happen. 

I intend to make a couple of these as long as we agree it's beneficial, but for now I want to keep these somewhat minimal and incremental. Hopefully this will make expanding autotuning capabilities less error prone and simple in the future.
